aliases.name: Fur-coat critter
aliases.meaning: informal description for the creature's lure

description.summary: A fearsome critter from American lumberjack tall tales, the Rumtifusel is a flat, mink-pelted predator that drapes itself over a stump like an abandoned fur coat to lure greedy passers-by, then drains them through suckers on its underside.
description.full: The Rumtifusel (also spelled Rumptifusel) belongs to the corpus of fearsome critters — humorous tall-tale beasts told in North American logging camps in the late 19th and early 20th centuries and catalogued in print by Henry H. Tryon in 'Fearsome Critters' (1939). It is described as large, flat, very flexible, and covered in a fine pelt resembling mink. The Rumtifusel hunts by mimicry: it drapes itself across a tree stump or fallen log so it looks like an expensive abandoned fur coat. When a 'tenderfoot' or other greedy passer-by approaches to claim the coat, the Rumtifusel — moving with deceptive speed — wraps around its victim. Its underside is lined with tiny suction pores that drain the victim until only bones remain. As with the rest of the fearsome-critter canon, the Rumtifusel is a humorous folkloric construct used for storytelling and the hazing of new lumberjacks rather than a claimed zoological animal.

etymology.origin: American English lumberjack slang of the early 20th century; published in Tryon (1939)
etymology.meaning: Onomatopoeic / nonsense compound; no agreed semantic gloss

features.description: Fine fur resembling that of a mink, valuable enough to tempt passers-by
Capable of draping over a stump or log so as to be mistaken for an abandoned fur coat
Tiny suction-like pores along the ventral surface that drain prey to the bone

physical.morphology: A flat, dorsoventrally flexible mammalian-pelted critter optimised in the tall tale for mimicry of an inert garment; no consistent skeletal anatomy is given.

abilities.description: Drapes over a stump to imitate a discarded expensive fur coat
Wraps around an approaching victim with deceptive speed
Drains body fluids through tiny suction pores until only bones remain

patterns: Operates by greed-based lure rather than active pursuit
Selects highly visible stumps and logs near trails

range.description: Within the lumberjack tall-tale tradition, the Rumtifusel is associated with the broad logging country of the northern United States and Canada — the same generic 'lumberwoods' setting that hosts most fearsome critters.

peak_activity_periods.description: Active circulation in published fearsome-critter folklore following Tryon's catalogue

origins.cultural_roots: Late-19th and early-20th-century North American lumberjack camp humour, where tall tales of bizarre creatures served to entertain crews and to haze 'tenderfoot' newcomers.
origins.earliest_accounts: Published account in Henry H. Tryon's 'Fearsome Critters' (Idlewild Press, 1939).
origins.folklore_connections: Part of the broader fearsome-critters canon: Roperite, Hidebehind, Agropelter, Hodag, Squonk, Splintercat, Wampus Cat, Side-hill Gouger, etc.

timeline.event: William T. Cox publishes 'Fearsome Creatures of the Lumberwoods', the first major print catalogue of the genre
timeline.significance: Establishes the fearsome-critters publishing tradition in which the Rumtifusel later appears

timeline.event: Henry H. Tryon's 'Fearsome Critters' is published, including the Rumtifusel entry
timeline.significance: Canonical first appearance of the Rumtifusel in print

history.modern_era: The Rumtifusel persists chiefly as a literary curiosity, frequently reprinted in folklore anthologies, cryptozoology bestiaries and contemporary illustrated revivals of the fearsome-critter genre.

documentary.name: Tryon 1939 entry on the Rumtifusel
documentary.description: Primary published account of the Rumtifusel in 'Fearsome Critters'.
documentary.analysis: Verified as a primary literary source within the fearsome-critters canon; the Rumtifusel has no claimed extra-literary existence.

skeptical.name: Lumberjack tall tale
skeptical.description: The Rumtifusel is a fictional creature invented for entertainment and for hazing greedy or naive newcomers. Its impossible anatomy and pure lure-and-drain hunting method are characteristic of the fearsome-critters genre.
proponents: Folklore scholars of the fearsome-critters tradition
evidence_cited: No physical evidence of any kind
Behaviour and morphology that violate known biology
Genre conventions of greed-punishing tall tales

traditions: North American lumberjack camp tall tales
stories: Tryon 1939 account of the fur-coat lure
folklore.beliefs: Understood by both tellers and audience as humorous fiction; the Rumtifusel functions as a moral tale about greed and unfamiliarity with the woods.

literature: Fearsome Creatures of the Lumberwoods: 20 Chilling Tales from the Wilderness — Hal Johnson (2015)
other: Routinely included in fearsome-critter art prints and online bestiaries

researchers.name: Henry H. Tryon
researchers.contribution: Author of 'Fearsome Critters' (1939), the canonical published source for the Rumtifusel

researchers.name: Hal Johnson
researchers.contribution: Modern illustrated revival of the fearsome-critter canon (2015)

research.ongoing_studies: None; treated as folklore literature rather than active cryptozoological inquiry.
